html:
Samuel Ajayi Crowther was a Yoruba linguist and clergyman who became the first African Anglican bishop, in 1864. As a boy he had been taken from a slave ship.

He was captured in about 1821, during the wars that were breaking up Oyo, and sold to Portuguese traders. In 1822 a ship of the British navy's West Africa Squadron, which enforced the ban on the slave trade, freed him and landed him at Freetown.

There he became a Christian, took the name Samuel Crowther, and was the first student enrolled at Fourah Bay College. He worked for the Church Missionary Society:

  • He joined British expeditions up the Niger in 1841 and after.
  • He wrote a Yoruba grammar and dictionary and led the translation of the Bible into Yoruba.
  • He found and was reunited with his mother in Abeokuta in the 1840s.

As bishop he led an African mission on the Niger. In his last years younger European missionaries pushed him and his African clergy aside, a turn that fed the rise of independent African churches.
sum: Samuel Ajayi Crowther was a Yoruba linguist and clergyman who became the first African Anglican bishop, in 1864. As a boy he had been taken from a slave ship.
